newsitem.title: Russia: Yeltsin, resting, remains out of public view.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, resting, remains out of public view.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, resting at a state residence outside Moscow after pneumonia, remained out of public view on Sunday nearly three weeks after his last official appearance.
The Kremlin played down concern over the 65-year-old president's health at the weekend, saying he was pushing ahead with plans to receive French President Jacques Chirac near Moscow next Sunday.

But Russian television has shown no new footage of Yeltsin since before he was taken to hospital on January 8, a longer gap even than the 15 days between his heart surgery on November 5 and his first television appearance after the operation.
"There is no new information. He is resting because it is not a working day," the presidential press office said.

Gerogy Satarov, a senior political aide to Yeltsin, told Interfax news agency that the president was "intellectually extremely active" but his attempts to rush his recovery had meant his absence from the Kremlim had dragged on.
"Of course he has to be strengthened physically, but intellectually and morally he feels great," Satarov said.
Yeltsin has been at the Gorky-9 residence outside Moscow since he was released from hospital on January 20 after 12 days of treatment for pneumonia of both lungs.

His latest illness, following the heart problems which forced him to spend nearly six months out of the Kremlin after his re-election last July, has prompted political opponents to demand his dismissal for health reasons.

"Boris Yeltsin should consider what his abilities are and not torment the country," said Gennady Zyuganov, leader of the opposition Communist Party, keeping up the pressure at a news conference in St Petersburg on Saturday.
The Kremlin has rebuffed demands to replace Yeltsin, saying they are unconstitutional.

Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday the president had not yet completed his recovery from pneumonia but was keen to return to full work and did not intened to scrap several planned foreign trips.
He also dismissed speculation on Saturday that Chirac's one-day visit to Russia on February 2 would be cancelled.
"President Boris Yeltsin has already started on direct preparations for the meeting with the President of France, Jacques Chirac," Yastrzhembsky told Interfax.
Yastrzhembsky has also scoffed at concern that no television pictures or new photographs of the president have appeared since he went down with pneumonia.

The lack of footage was particularly striking last Wednesday, when Yastrzhembsky said Yeltisn went to the Kremlin for talks with Prime Minster Viktor Chernomyrdin. Television channels simply showed still photographs or old footage.

"Do we not understand the meaning of the television sideshows when, instead of a "live' conversation between Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin, they show us two photographs of these esteemed men and say behind the pictures that they discussed current problems?" the opposition Sovietskaya Rossiya newspaper said on Saturday. "We understand very well what this means."

Yeltsin has kept silent on parliamentary and presidential elections on Monday in the Chechnya region, where he sent troops to smash an indepedence drive in 1994 only to agree to their humiliating withdrawal after 21 months of fighting.

Russian deputy foreign minister Viktor Posuvalyuk told Interfax that Moscow was ready to break off ties with any country that granted diplomatic recognition to Chechnya. It was not clear if this was official Kremlin policy.
